B.assessment: Complete brief establishes three uint8 bands, nodata metadata and some external .msk files; neither actual values/flags nor algorithm band requirements are given. Six obligations and bounded delivery conditions apply.

S01.assessment: List-index read_masks has shape (bands, rows, columns); dataset_mask returns a 2D mask.

S02.assessment: Executable dataset_mask directly returns band-1 mask if band-1 flags contain per_dataset; otherwise count==4 and first color red selects band-4 MASK; otherwise logical OR of returned band masks, normalized to 0/255. Nodata is not itself a Python branch test.

S03.assessment: GDAL mask zero is invalid; any nonzero is valid. Masked reads cast bytes to bool and invert that validity, so masked-array True is invalid.

S04.assessment: per_dataset means shared across bands. Recognized external masks may instead have one mask band per image band; a recognized sidecar alone does not establish the direct dataset_mask branch.

S05.assessment: Corresponding recognized .msk masks precede nodata-derived masks for affected bands. Recognition requires a valid GDAL dataset, naming/band-count and INTERNAL_MASK_FLAGS_xx metadata; missing flags can leave a band on fallback. Existence alone is insufficient.

S06.assessment: Writing/using mask validity does not itself rewrite samples or nodata metadata. Rasterio write_mask creates/uses a shared mask on band 1.

S07.assessment: The guide gives a possible 16-bit-to-8-bit rounding collision with zero nodata. It does not establish these survey tiles were scaled or have nodata zero. Values alone cannot distinguish stored zeros with different original meanings.

S08.assessment: Guide byte-reconstruction identity is accurately quoted. Boolean conversion discards valid mask intensities 1..254; reconstruction yields 255. Exact byte equality needs canonical 0/255 masks; inverse boolean validity is general.

S09.assessment: Shared write_mask limitation does not prohibit a generic independently differing external-mask fixture: GDAL describes N-band external masks and band-level creation without per_dataset. This is a source-contract possibility, not an executed driver witness.

S10.assessment: All-valid no-nodata fallback assumes no applicable explicit/alpha mask. In the stated no-nodata/no-mask three-band fixture, each fallback band mask is 255 and OR remains 255.

S11.assessment: np.all with axis=0 and logical_and.reduce with its default axis=0 both reduce the selected-band dimension of a boolean array.

S12.assessment: The guide uses an empirically chosen sieve size in its example. That supports neither an automatic repair of unknown survey masks nor a universal ban on evidence-supported sieving.
